newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Gambian military leader predicts poll victory.
newsitem.headline: Gambian military leader predicts poll victory.

text.p: Gambian military leader Yahya Jammeh, who has resigned from the army to run in presidential elections this month, predicted on Thursday that he would win 99 percent of the vote.
"I am optimistic I will win the forthcoming elections on September 26 by 99 percent and one percent will go to charity for my opponents," Jammeh, 31, told reporters after filing his nomination.
Jammeh, who seized power in a 1994 coup as a U.S.-trained army captain, resigned on August 28 along with four associates in his provisional ruling council, the official gazette said.
Military sources said he had been promoted to the rank of colonel at the time of his resignation and would remain the commander-in-chief of the West African country's armed forces.
Asked how he felt as a civilian, Jammeh said: "Once a soldier you are always a soldier. I have the profession at heart."

Jammeh's most serious electoral rival, lawyer Ousainou Darboe of the United Democratic Party (UDP), demanded a transitional government to run the elections. He said he was considering a legal challenge to the continuing presence of Jammeh and his fellow retired officers on the ruling council.
"Legally and constitutionally they cannot be part of the Armed Forces Provisional Ruling Council," Darboe said after filing his own nomination, trailed by hundreds of supporters.
"We want everything done according to law and I will brief my lawyer about this anomaly. We should have an interim civil government," said Darboe, 48, vice-president of the Gambian Bar Association.

The military government lifted a two-year ban on politics on August 14. The 1994 coup that toppled the elected government of Sir Dawda Jawara was condemned by Western donors whose pressure forced Jammeh to speed up the transition to civilian rule.
He has has banned the country's main politicians from standing but will be challenged by Darboe and two other civilian candidates.
Many politicians banned by Jammeh from contesting the election because of their association with Jawara have flocked to Darboe's party along with their supporters.

The small People's Democratic Organisation for Independence and Socialism is putting up Sidia Jatta, who polled 5.6 percent in presidential elections in 1992 won by Jawara. The fourth contender is Amath Bah, a manager at a hotel in Serekunda.
Thursday was the deadline for the filing of nominations. Candidates deposited the equivalent of $1,000 each along with 5,000 signatures and a declaration of assets.
Jammeh registered as a candidate of the Alliance for Patriotic Reorientation and Construction formed by him and military associates.
